ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** Both sections cover the same opening (Europa mission, the Ada Limón poem excerpt, water's centrality to life, the reveal that the origin remains uncertain), and the full historical arc: comets, the isotopic mismatch, Ashley King's 'fell out of favor' quote, the shift to asteroids, the asteroid model's own problems, and the pivot to the endogenous idea. No substantive idea from the expected section is missing.

A Showdown Between Comets and Asteroids:
**1:** Both sections cover the 4.54-billion-year formation framing, comets as early frontrunner (Kuiper Belt/Oort cloud, Bryson's 'bang for buck' quote), the D/H diagnostic (Giotto/Halley's ~2x mismatch, Meech's 'didn't match at all' quote -- the expected section's exact quote, unlike several other presets/replicates of this article), the Hale-Bopp and Rosetta/67P confirmations, the asteroid case (Winchcombe, Hayabusa2/Ryugu), the noble-gas shortcoming, and the Late Heavy Bombardment problem. The generated section omits Ashley King's second quote ('the community is probably more favorable of asteroids...') -- the underlying claim that asteroids are now favored is still conveyed narratively, so this is a dropped quote rather than a missing idea. The section also adds a well-sourced elaboration on the Nice model and a quantified comet-delivery-fraction estimate -- see depth_enhancement.

Hydrogen, Meet Magma:
**1:** Both sections cover the exoplanet-hydrogen framing, the enstatite-chondrite reevaluation (including all three hydrogen-hiding-place items), the 2023 theoretical proposal, the magma-ocean mechanism, the diamond-anvil-cell experiments, Sang-Heon Shim's 'we broke a lot of diamonds' quote, Paul Byrne's quotes, H. W. Horn's 'right on the edge' quote, Anders Johansen's skepticism (named and paraphrased rather than directly quoted), the 'water factory for a brief period' framing, and the 'born water-rich' habitability implication. Quentin Williams is not named. No substantive idea is otherwise missing, and the section adds a well-sourced, higher-magnitude water-yield figure and a snow-line-breaking implication -- see depth_enhancement.

Drowning in a Sea of Possibilities:
**1:** Both sections cover the limited cometary resurgence (the 2011 Herschel Hartley 2 measurement, the 2024 dust-contamination reanalysis of 67P, and the 2025 12P/Pons-Brooks detection), Karen Meech's 'combination of all of them' quote, a mixed-source synthesis, the complicating post-delivery factors, and a closing parallel to origin-of-life research. The generated section omits Meech's 'We may never know' quote specifically -- the underlying idea (isotopic erasure makes a single source hard to identify) is still stated -- and its closing quote reads 'richer and more complex' rather than the expected section's exact 'richer and more exciting,' which I want to flag as a verbatim misquotation rather than a paraphrase (it is presented in quotation marks as Meech's exact words). Neither omission removes a substantive idea, so this scores 1, but see the note at the end of this response on the altered quote.
